articles.title: ASRA Q. NOMANI: Old-guard Dems face Frankenstein moment as leftists come for them
articles.summary: Last Thursday, Ben Cohen and CodePink packed a House Longworth Building office demanding an end to the Iran war as activists turn on Democratic leaders.
articles.body: WASHINGTON, D.C. — Ice cream magnate Ben Cohen and activists from the far-left nonprofit CodePink packed into a lawmaker's office in House Longworth Building Room 1236 last week, demanding an end to the war in Iran, a cutoff of U.S. military ties to Israel and the removal of Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth. Next door, in House Rayburn Building Room 2267, Capitol police officers arrested far-left, anti-Israel demonstrators, including prolific street theater activist Hazami Barmada, cloaked in symbolic blood red, as they packed another lawmaker's office, condemning complicity in Israel's alleged "genocide" of Palestinians in Gaza. Across Capitol Hill in Senate Hart Building Room 322, police officers arrested young adults from a far-left nonprofit and political action committee, Sunrise Movement, as they packed a senator's office, condemning his politics, including his support of Israel. The next day, an activist from a far-left nonprofit, Climate Defiance, screamed at a high-ranking lawmaker speaking at a political conference, calling him a "traitor." But they weren't going after Republican lawmakers. They were far-left activists with a special target: The Democratic Party's leadership. JEFFRIES BRUSHES OFF OPPOSITION FROM FAR-LEFT DEMS WHO VOTED NO: 'WE’RE GOING TO WORK TOGETHER' The target of Cohen, the co-founder of Ben and Jerry's, was California Democratic Rep. Nancy Pelosi, former speaker of the House. The anti-Israel protesters had filled the office of Democratic Rep. Hakeem Jeffries of New York, nominated Wednesday by fellow Democrats to be the next House speaker despite the protests. The Sunrise Movement agitators had flooded the office of top Senate Democrat Chuck Schumer, and the activists of Climate Defiance were attempting to shame Jeffries at a conference of the Democratic Party. The groups protesting top Democrats represent the full spectrum of a "red-green-green-blue" alliance – made up of socialist and pro-communist "red" organizations, Muslim and Arab "green" groups, environmental "green" activists and traditional "blue" groups. The alliance has emerged in recent years to press a far-left agenda in U.S. politics, particularly on the issue of ending U.S. support for Israel. A Fox News Digital investigation reveals that 22 groups from the network – harnessing about $342 million in annual revenues – are now waging a coordinated effort, dubbed "CHUCK CHUCK," aimed at ousting Schumer from his expected role as Senate majority leader, creating the myth of the marching millions with shared messaging, social media campaigns, influencer videos and staged arrests. The campaign is operating on several fronts: activists "bird-dogging" lawmakers in the halls of Congress, national advocacy organizations endorsing Maryland Sen. Chris Van Hollen over Schumer, local chapters organizing demonstrations and supporters mobilizing phone calls to senators ahead of a Dec. 1 secret-ballot leadership election. On Monday, Brooklyn activists from a traditionally Democratic group, Indivisible Project, plan to "celebrate" Schumer's 76th birthday with a protest against him at his Third Avenue midtown Manhattan office. Schumer maintains that he has the votes to win, and he most likely does. A Fox News Digital anti-Schumer tracker shows that Van Hollen only has the support of five sitting or incoming senators: Bernie Sanders, Abdul El-Sayed, Jeff Merkley, Peggy Flanagan and himself. But he does have 22 organizations fueling and amplifying the anti-Schumer campaign to win more votes. So far, they include: SCHUMER BOASTS EARLY ADVANTAGE IN SENATE POWER STRUGGLE AS DEM RIVAL WARNS AGAINST 'CORONATION' The emerging dynamics are reminiscent of the Frankenstein story, with the Democratic establishment empowering the powerful activist movement to defeat its Republican opponents. But now, parts of that movement are turning on the very political establishment that helped bring them to power. Earlier this year, the Sunrise Movement's executive director, Aru Shiney-Ajay, led an online discussion, published on YouTube, headlined "How to Take Over the Democratic Party." Neera Tanden, a longtime ally of Bill and Hillary Clinton and now executive director of the Center for American Progress, a Democratic nonprofit created by former Clinton administration chief of staff John Podesta, has another term for the rebels from within who challenge Jeffries: "chaos agents." On Tuesday, she wrote on X, "I personally would like the names of everyone who wins an historic election and then immediately goes into a circular firing squad so we can tag the chaos agents for the future." Meanwhile, witnessing the targeting of Jeffries as a "traitor," Texas Democratic Party advisor Kurt Bardella wrote on X, "I can tell you there are times when the tactics and venom coming from the activist left are completely indistinguishable to the MAGA right. They just come off as unhinged a--holes who are throwing tantrums." PROGRESSIVES FACE ACCUSATIONS OF RACISM OVER ATTACKS ON HAKEEM JEFFRIES AS HE SEEKS SPEAKERSHIP When Code Pink co-founder Medea Benjamin emerged from Pelosi's office last week, trailing behind Capitol Police officers called by staffers to assess the situation, she told Fox News Digital: "See, we're bipartisan. We yell at Democrats as much as we yell and scream at Republicans." Importantly, for some of them, the goal of the "red" in the red-green-green-blue alliance isn't Western free-enterprise democracy. Benjamin's fellow CodePink co-founder, Jodie Evans, gave Fox News Digital a more ideological explanation for rejecting Democrats alongside Republicans, as she stood outside Pelosi's office. "I'm a socialist, because I believe in equality, so I teach it. It's the peace economy," Evans said. "Socialism is the peace of economy. I read Marx to try to understand why we were at war with communists. Like, well, how bad were they?... They wanted equality for everyone! What insanity!" The encounters last week captured a fault line running through the opposition to President Donald Trump. Some activists want to push the Democratic Party further left. Others who are openly pro-socialist and pro-communist reject both major parties and see a Democratic victory as another opportunity to organize against the political establishment. QUIET PART OUT LOUD: ANTI-ISRAEL MOBS WANT ONE STATE CALLED 'PALESTINE,' ERASING ISRAEL Most importantly, a connective thread runs through the protests by the "red-green-green-blue" alliance: anti-Israel messaging. Within the broader pro-Palestinian movement, activists advocate different goals, including a Palestinian "right of return" to Israel, a single democratic "one state" encompassing Israel and the Palestinian territories, an end to "Zionism" and Israel's status as a Jewish state, and the emergence of a "free, free Palestine" "from the river to the sea." Proponents of a "one-state" solution argue that Palestinians and their descendants displaced following Israel's creation in 1948 should be permitted the "right of return" and receive "equal rights" in Israel. Critics contend that such a demographic transformation would end Israel's character as a Jewish homeland. Supporters invoke "rules-based international law" to describe their proposals as a framework for "human rights," "equal rights" and "self-determination" for Palestinians. These fissures with centrist Democrats are being expressed by the leaders of groups including CodePink, BreakThrough BT Media, the People's Forum and Tricontinental, funded by American-born communist tycoon Neville Roy Singham, who lives in Shanghai, supporting the Chinese Communist Party. CodePink's Evans is married to Singham. Congressional investigators and Justice Department prosecutors have investigated Singham's activities and funding as possible malign foreign influence. No charges have been filed against Singham or the groups he has funded. SCHUMER'S LEADERSHIP RIVAL REVEALS MAJOR SENATE RULE CHANGE HE'D PURSUE IF ELECTED Even with Jeffries' leadership survival, their targets include the two Democrats positioned to lead the incoming congressional Democratic majority – Schumer and Jeffries – with disputes over U.S. support for Israel among the grievances raised by activists interviewed by Fox News Digital. The confrontations harken back to the protests surrounding the 2024 Democratic National Convention in Chicago, where demonstrators gathered at Union Park and marched toward the convention, denouncing Vice President Kamala Harris as "Killer Kamala" and President Joe Biden as "Genocide Joe" for supporting Israel in its campaign against Hamas' Oct. 7, 2023, attack on Israel. Some of the same organizations and activists challenging Democrats today were gathered in Union Park back then. Two years later, Democrats’ midterm victories have brought another round of demands, demonstrations and threats to withhold support from Democratic Party leaders. In an April 2025 interview with New York magazine, Alexander Soros, son of billionaire Democratic Party funder George Soros, expressed his frustration with the leftist environmentalist group Sunrise Movement, which has been heavily funded by Soros organizations. "What the hell did they do, by the way?" Soros said in the interview. "We gave them money, and now all they do is talk about Palestine. It’s ridiculous." ALEX SOROS FUMES AT LEFT-WING CLIMATE GROUP OVER 'PALESTINE' OBSESSION The dynamics of the "chaos agents" ramped up even as votes were still being counted from the Democratic Party's "blue tsunami" wins in the midterm elections. On Nov. 4, the day after the election, BreakThrough News host Rania Khalek, in D.C. last week for lobbying organized by CodePink, led a panel discussion with co-host Zoe Alexandra featuring the top Singham network personalities — BreakThrough News editor-in-chief Ben Becker; People's Forum executive director Manolo De Los Santos; and Tricontinental executive director Vijay Prashad — blasting the Democrats. That day, the Democratic Socialists of America declared that voters had "emphatically endorsed socialism" and urged Americans to reject "the complacent center and the fascist right." The next day, BreakThrough published a Khalek segment titled "Schumer & Jeffries reap the backlash to the genocide they enabled," accusing the Democratic leaders of benefiting politically from opposition to policies they had helped sustain. Khalek followed the next day with a written appeal linking to her "BT Live" segment. She accused Democratic leaders of serving wealthy interests and argued that sustained organizing could force policy concessions. "Do not go back to brunch. Get organized," she wrote. Also on Nov. 5, Our Revolution, a 501(c)(4) political nonprofit backed by Sen. Bernie Sanders, an elder statesman revered by members of the Democratic Socialists of America, made clear that its leadership challenge extended to both chambers. "Real question: how do people calling for Schumer to step down justify giving Hakeem Jeffries a pass?" the group posted. By Saturday, Nov. 7, that pressure was visible on Manhattan’s streets. Demonstrators marched from Times Square toward Seventh Avenue and 14th Street in a rally organized by groups including the Democratic Socialists of America’s New York City chapter. The protests were cast as anti-Trump but there was another theme in the crowd: anti-Democratic Party. Among their chants: "Jeffries, Schumer let’s be clear, ICE is not wanted here." Demonstrators held signs reading, "Remove Jeffries / Schumer" and "CALL JEFFRIES & SCHUMER / TELL THEM TO STEP ASIDE." One sign repeated the thread of anti-Israel activism, aimed also at the pro-Israel lobbying group, the American Israel Public Affairs Committee: "They are not capable of meeting this moment. We need FIGHTERS with BACKBONE & VISION – not corporate & AIPAC hacks." By Sunday, Nov. 8, the Party for Socialism and Liberation, a communist group working out of the headquarters of the People's Forum on Wesr 37th Street in Manhattan, attacked Schumer directly. "Chuck Schumer isn’t an ‘architect’ of anything except the genocide in Gaza," the organization wrote, adding that Schumer had no place leading a Senate "which should be abolished anyway." CHAOS INC.: COMMUNISTS, ANTIFA, AGITATORS IN THE RED-GREEN ALLIANCE By early last week, the pressure campaign had reached Schumer’s and Jeffries' offices. At 12:51 p.m. on Tuesday, Nov. 10, CodePink's Benjamin tried to enter Schumer's office in Hart Room 322, and posted a video with the message: "Chuck Schumer locked his office on us!" The next day, at 10:35 a.m., the activists reached Jeffries' office in Rayburn Room 2267 and Benjamin recorded a staged statement outside the door for CodePink's social media account. On Thursday, Nov. 12, Barmada, wearing her red costume, joined a new confrontation at Jeffries’ office, filming as Capitol Police escorted other activists away. Iran's state-run Press TV later promoted the protest on its anti-U.S. propaganda platform. Barmada didn't respond to a request for comment. Across the Capitol complex, at 2:55 p.m., Schumer's staff faced the sit-in staged by Sunrise Movement's protest organizers, chanting on script, "Hey hey, ho ho, Schumer has got to go!" Capitol Police arrested 54 activists during the Sunrise Movement action, and a battalion of influencers splashed the news across social media in a series of similar posts. ASRA NOMANI: EL-SAYED GLIDES INTO ROLE AS ROCK STAR OF THE HARD LEFT'S RED-GREEN ALLIANCE By Thursday night, amid the coordinated campaign by the left, the campaign to replace Schumer had a declared candidate. Van Hollen announced he would seek the majority leader’s job, and El-Sayed endorsed him. Just days earlier, El-Sayed had smiled quietly as the board president of the Arab America Foundation led a supportive crowd in chants of "Free, free Palestine," "from the river to the sea." El-Sayed previously served on the board of the Sunrise Movement, whose organizers have been demanding Schumer's removal. The relationship illustrates how the pressure campaign extends beyond street demonstrations to elected Democrats with histories in activist organizations. That day, Democratic Socialists of America published a message, "SAY NO TO SCHUMER," over images of the leader. Soon after, the "World Socialist Web Site," representing a pro-communist "world Trotskyist movement" and "Marxist world outlook," promoted the "SAY NO TO SCHUMER" campaign, touting Van Hollen as a "lifelong servant of the Democratic establishment." The next day, CodePink's D.C. organizer, Olivia DiNucci, regularly seen heckling public officials and lawmakers, responded with a triumphant video, calling on activists to lobby against Schumer in the halls of Congress and flood congressional officials with the message: "VOTE CHRIS, NOT CHUCK." And, wearing a hot pink T-shirt with the graphic of a watermelon, a quirky symbol of Palestinian "resistance," and "Falasteen," the Arabic word for a Palestinian homeland, CodePink's Benjamin responded that day by urging support for Van Hollen, citing as her first reason: "He has been a forceful critic of Israel's assault on Palestinians." The campaign to oust Schumer is now drawing support from two of the Democratic Party’s most established "progressive" political nonprofits: Indivisible Project and MoveOn.org Civic Action, both 501(c)(4) nonprofits. Indivisible Project says it opposes Schumer's "coronation," and Indivisible Brooklyn is promoting an "Even New Yorkers Don’t Want Chuck" week of action, including a Times Square rally on Thursday, co-sponsored by other Indivisible chapters. MoveOn reports that 75% of participating members who voted support Van Hollen. Meanwhile, last Friday, Barmada posted a video with one of the activists arrested at Jeffries’ office. She wore a T-shirt that said, "FREE AMERICA FROM ISRAEL," with the image of an Israeli flag over the mouth of the Statue of Liberty. The back of her shirt read: "ISRAEL GETS BILLIONS / AMERICANS PAY THE BILL." She accused Jeffries of being "a mouthpiece for Israel, AIPAC, the Israeli lobby," and declared: "The Democrats are spineless." After the vote paving the way for Jeffries to become House speaker Wednesday, the activists in the red-green-green-blue alliance weren't relenting in their anti-Schumer campaign. At 2:05 p.m., the Council on American-Islamic Relations issued an "Action Alert" to support Van Hollen against "AIPAC's toxic influence over our politics." The appeal followed an endorsement of Van Hollen by the U.S. Council of Muslim Organizations, an umbrella coalition of American Muslim institutions. At 4:49 p.m., a far-left 501(c)(4) political nonprofit, Showing Up for Racial Justice, which organizes "white people for racial and economic justice," announced it is hosting phone banks to "FIRE CHUCK." Around then, Sunrise Movement posted a video of actor Mark Ruffalo, speaking to the camera as he blasted Schumer's support of an environmental bill, gripping his forehead with his hands and saying, "God bless him," as he spoke about Schumer. A follower responded: "Sorry folks but red and blue are two sides of the same bloody coin." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

articles.title: Thune on midterms: GOP candidates didn’t have ‘much control over’ key voter issues
articles.summary: Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-S.D.) says Republicans lost nine Senate seats in the midterms because they had no control over the issues that most impacted voters, including the Iran war, gas prices and inflation. He also suggested the political headwinds caused by President Trump’s decision to go to war sunk GOP chances to win.…
articles.body:
Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-S.D.) says Republicans lost nine Senate seats in the midterms because they had no control over the issues that most impacted voters, including the Iran war, gas prices and inflation.

He also suggested the political headwinds caused by President Trump’s decision to go to war sunk GOP chances to win.

“Any exit poll that you look at would tell you it was about the war, it was about the economy, it was about inflation, it was about gas prices. I think that’s what it came down to, none of which our candidates had much control over,” Thune told John Roberts, the anchor of Fox News’s “America Reports.”

Thune noted independent voters shifted decisively away from Republican candidates in this month’s election, something that polls shared within the Senate GOP conference months earlier showed would likely happen.

“The things that we can control going forward are to ensure that we are talking to those voters, the middle of the electorate, those independent voters who broke against us by 30 points — I mean, we lost independents, which represent a third of the electorate, in all those key Senate races by 30 percentage points,” the South Dakota Republican continued.

“We got to start delivering an economic message about the cost of living, the things the American people care about,” he added.

Thune noted Republicans can recapture the Senate majority if they “win the hearts and minds of the American people.”

“That means coming up with a compelling economic message, talking about secure streets, secure borders — safe streets — and more money in your pocket,” he said. “Those are the things the American people care the most about.”

National exit polls showed that only 38 percent of voters who cast ballots in the midterm election approved of Trump’s job performance , and only 36 percent said they think Trump “fights for people like you.”

The surveys also found that 63 percent of voters blamed the president for higher prices .

Senate Republicans will have a tough electoral map in 2028 as they will need to defend 19 GOP-held seats while Democrats will need to defend 16 Democratic-held seats.

articles.body:
President Trump on Thursday said he thinks he’ll be more productive with the incoming Democratic Congress than he was with the GOP-led one over the first two years of his second term.

“And I have a feeling that this is going to be an unbelievably productive two years. They’ll send me — well, they’ll send me a bill on healthcare, and I’ll say, ‘No way,’ and I’ll veto it. And then they’ll call me and they’ll say — and we’ll sit down. And that’s what I do,” Trump told Fox News’s Jacqui Heinrich in an interview that aired on “The Ingraham Angle.”

“You’ll have them at the White House, soon?” Heinrich asked Trump.

“Sure, I’ll have — I respect them, they won. Politics is a nasty game, and they won,” the president replied. “And I don’t agree with everything, but I will say this: I think I can do, in many ways, better now.”

Democrats won the House and Senate in the midterm elections earlier this month, making notable gains in regions where they have historically struggled to win, like Texas and Kansas. The GOP faced an uphill battle, with issues like the unpopular war in Iran, Trump’s slumping approval ratings and concerns about the cost of living weighing heavy on voters.

Last week, Trump voiced distaste with the work of Senate Republicans, calling their actions “devastating” to the GOP and saying their lack of action caused the party’s losses in the midterms.

“The Republican Senate can no longer be the place ‘where things are sent to die.’ Not passing THE SAVE AMERICA ACT (Voter I.D., Proof of Citizenship), sent up five times by the House, was devastating to the Republican Party in the Midterms,” Trump wrote last week.

articles.title: Jeffries warns Democrats ready to investigate ‘everyone’ in ‘MAGA extremist movement’
articles.summary: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-N.Y.) is warning that Democrats are prepared to investigate “everyone” in the “MAGA extremist movement” when his party takes control of the House in the next Congress. “Everyone who has been part of this MAGA extremist movement that has unleashed all of this carnage and damage on the American people…
articles.body:
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-N.Y.) is warning that Democrats are prepared to investigate “everyone” in the “MAGA extremist movement” when his party takes control of the House in the next Congress.

“Everyone who has been part of this MAGA extremist movement that has unleashed all of this carnage and damage on the American people should be prepared to answer questions as it relates to what has happened, why it’s happened and, of course, from our view, how do we prevent this type of carnage from ever happening again?” Jeffries said Wednesday evening in an interview with MS NOW’s Jen Psaki.

Jeffries, who’s in line to become Speaker next year when the House changes hands, did not define a “MAGA extremist,” nor did he name names. But his warning is consistent with the Democrats’ promises to cast a wide net of investigations into President Trump, his Cabinet, his family and his allies when they take the gavels in the 120th Congress.

Jeffries has spent much of the past two years accusing Trump and his allies of unprecedented corruption, including efforts to use their positions of power to enrich themselves and their families.

But the latest warning takes on new resonance after this month’s midterm rout, which gave Democrats a huge majority with which to conduct their investigations, and Wednesday’s vote of the House Democratic Caucus, which nominated Jeffries to become the next Speaker.

Psaki, a former Biden administration official, was asking specifically about potential investigations into Elon Musk, the tech mogul and Trump supporter who has taken steps this week to distance himself from the MAGA movement in the wake of the Republicans’ clobbering in the midterm elections.

Jeffries didn’t bite, deferring the specific targets of any probes to the Democrats who are set to chair the various investigative committees, including Rep. Jamie Raskin (D-Md.) on the House Judiciary Committee and Robert Garcia (D-Calif.) on the Oversight and Government Reform Committee.

But he also pointed to Musk’s role as the head of the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) last year, when DOGE officials sought to slash trillions of dollars from federal programs championed by Democrats.

“He was the individual who held up a chainsaw and began the process of trying to detonate things like Social Security and Medicare and perhaps setting in motion what occurred in that one big ugly bill,” Jeffries said.

Other Democrats, including Garcia, have gone a long step further, vowing already that Musk will be a target of their investigations.

articles.title: Quote of the day by Plato- “In politics we presume that everyone who knows how to get votes knows how to…”
articles.summary: Some people consider a person's looks or charm their number one priority when choosing a partner, while others might have different considerations.
articles.body: Some people consider a person's looks or charm their number one priority when choosing a partner, while others might have different considerations. While choosing a romantic partner, these preferences are extremely personal and affect only the people involved. But would you accept the promotion of a colleague who is not as competent as you but has immense charm? The seniors overlook mistakes in their work just because they are able to joke around the office. However, the assumption that a charming person is also the one who can get the work done doesn't always hold true.The quote of the day by Plato, “In politics we presume that everyone who knows how to get votes knows how to administer a city or a state. When we are ill... we do not ask for the handsomest physician, or the most eloquent one” also highlights this.What does the quote really mean?Plato's idea comes from The Republic, where Socrates compares running a state to steering a ship. In his picture, the captain is strong but a little deaf, a little blind and not very good at sailing, while the sailors fight to take the wheel even though they know nothing of navigation. They flatter whoever helps them win control, and they dismiss the real navigator as a useless stargazer, though he alone knows how to find the right course.The story is not about the voters being foolish. It basically creates a distinction between the skill of running things and winning people over. A great orator who can charm the voter base through his wonderful speeches may not know how to act in a crisis. A great-looking person may not be the best surgeon or the best pilot. However, the skill might just lie with someone who quietly sits in a corner.Why does it matter today?Administering a state is a complex task which requires an understanding of various facets of governance, law and humanity. The responsibility has to be performed with values of empathy, compassion and non-partisanship embodied rather than imposed. Heads of state are made to take oaths of integrity, yet no country is free of corruption. They make great speeches about the need to maintain peace around the world, yet every country keeps increasing its defence budgets. Under the welfare state system, governments keep talking about providing for the weak and minorities, yet inequality persists.These contradictions highlight how the democracy that we so love might not be working very well for us. Plato lived in a time without television, let alone social media. Today, we scroll through short clips, sharp one-liners and perfectly polished images. A confident voice can travel to millions in minutes, while thoughtful choices often remain hidden. This is being adopted even by politicians. The populism we observe today has far greater reach than it used to. Today, a powerful speech by a politician suddenly makes them a global leader. This charm is often noticed by the people who vote for them as well. They rely on propaganda that is highly emotive and reaches the majority, leading to election victories. Populism wins, yet it does not bring a change to the common man's life, who got honey-trapped by the charm of a politician seeking power.The quote does not tell us to distrust good speakers. It only wants us to reflect on how people do not always have to be the most charming for them to know a skill. This is especially important in politics, as the stakes are high. Politicians decide the future of a country where millions of people may depend on the government even for their basic needs.A lesson for all of usPerhaps the best lesson here is that good choices take effort. Pausing before we cheer, checking before we believe and thinking before we vote are small habits, but a society is built from small habits.And it asks something of leaders too. Real leadership is less like winning applause and more like being the navigator: studying the stars, keeping the ship steady and caring about everyone on board, even when no one is clapping.After all, we do not want a doctor who only sounds good. We want one who heals. Perhaps we should ask the same of everyone who steers our shared ship.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ testGet the latest Lifestyle News and more. articles.summary: Every day of delay has consequences. Women like Herring and their unborn children deserve protection now — not more bureaucratic excuses and endless delays.
articles.body:
Catherine Pressly Herring was pregnant with her third child when her husband secretly slipped one of the drugs used in chemical abortion into her drinks in an attempt to cause an abortion without her knowledge. He did it repeatedly.

Catherine became violently ill and began bleeding. Her daughter survived but was born 10 weeks premature. Her husband eventually pleaded guilty to assault of a pregnant person and injury to a child. He was sentenced to 180 days in jail and 10 years of probation. After later violating a protective order, his probation was revoked and he was sentenced to eight years in prison.

In October, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration provided a court-ordered update on the safety review of the chemical abortion drug mifepristone. In it, the report release date was postponed until March 2027. The administration has been dragging its feet on needed action on the abortion pill for more than a year.

The FDA should pull the abortion pill from the market. At the very least, the administration should end mail-order abortion until a permanent solution is in place. Millions of unborn children have already lost their lives through chemical abortion, and it is far past time to act.

In fact, the available data show the abortion pill is not safe and effective as labeled today. Chemical abortion now accounts for about 65 percent of human lives ended by abortion in the U.S., according to the Guttmacher Institute’s current national data. In 2020, the figure was 53 percent.

Those percentages represent millions of dead American children.

The FDA approves mifepristone as part of the chemical abortion regimen through 10 weeks of pregnancy. By that point, the child has already undergone weeks of rapid development. Her arms and legs are taking shape, her fingers and toes are visible, and her major organ systems have begun developing.

The abortion pill Mifepristone blocks progesterone, a hormone needed to sustain the pregnancy. Misoprostol is then taken to cause contractions and expel the child. The purpose of the two-drug regimen is abortion: to end the child’s life.

Over the last two decades, the FDA has tragically made these drugs easier and easier to obtain. Mifepristone was originally approved in 2000 with far more restrictive rules. In 2016, the FDA extended approved use from the first seven weeks of pregnancy to 10 weeks and loosened other requirements. The agency later eliminated the in-person dispensing requirement, so that abortion pills can now be prescribed remotely and sent through the mail.

An individual can now receive abortion drugs without ever sitting in the same room as the doctor prescribing them.

There is also crucial evidence about the risks women face. The Ethics and Public Policy Center conducted the largest study on the real-world effect of the abortion pill by analyzing insurance claims associated with 865,727 prescribed mifepristone abortions from 2017 through 2023. It found that nearly 11 percent involved what it classified as serious adverse events within 45 days, including sepsis, infection and hemorrhaging.

My organization investigated how Planned Parenthood sent out these abortion pills with no safeguards. At multiple locations across the country, investigators were told women could obtain mifepristone through telehealth without even an ultrasound to confirm gestational age. Without that screening, an ectopic pregnancy can go undetected. Abortion pills do not treat ectopic pregnancies — a rupture can cause catastrophic internal bleeding and even death.

Failure to confirm gestational age can also mean women take the drugs much later in pregnancy, increasing the risks of severe hemorrhage, infection, and other serious complications. Multiple facilities even said that the pills could be mailed to someone else’s home and kept for later use. The investigation exposed a reckless system distributing powerful abortion drugs with remarkably little medical oversight, leaving women vulnerable to dangerous and potentially life-threatening complications

Catherine Herring’s case makes that danger impossible to dismiss — nor is it by any means the only one (in the U.S. or abroad ) in which abortion drugs are being weaponized against women and their children in utero by people who had no business acquiring them. Every abortion kills a baby, and in many cases like Catherine’s, it is also a crime against the mother.

Planned Parenthood’s latest annual report shows the enormous scale of its operation: 434,450 abortions during its last fiscal year and approximately $832 million in government health-services reimbursements and grants.

From the outside, it appears political considerations are influencing the timing of abortion-related decisions inside the administration. Now the election has come and gone, and the mifepristone safety report has still not been released. If election strategy shaped that timetable, it intruded on decisions that should be governed by evidence, law and the administration’s responsibility to protect the public.

And the delay continues. In its Oct. 7 court filing, the FDA acknowledged that it expects study results by mid-December, yet it does not plan to finish its report until March 2027. There are additional concerns that the study itself will be inconclusive due to a lack of Medicaid data.

Every day of delay has consequences. Women like Herring and their unborn children deserve protection now — not more bureaucratic excuses and endless delays.

Congress must act now, because pro-abortion leadership takes control in January, and the next FDA commissioner must make a commitment to all Americans, including preborn children.

Withdraw mifepristone for abortion. At a minimum, end mail-order abortion immediately — no more delays, no more excuses.

Lila Rose is the president and founder of the national pro-life organization Live Action .

articles.title: AOC leaves door open to 2028 presidential run, signals willingness to work with Trump
articles.summary: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez would not rule out a 2028 White House run, saying her focus is getting results for people after Democrats reclaimed the House majority.
articles.body: Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., is leaving the door open to a potential 2028 presidential bid as speculation grows over her political future. "I think, right now, this election just happened. We got to work on getting results for people," Ocasio-Cortez told Fox News Digital when asked whether she was considering a presidential run in 2028. The self-described democratic socialist also expressed a willingness to work with President Donald Trump on key legislative priorities as Democrats prepare to take control of the House following the 2026 midterm elections. PROGRESSIVE ORG LAUNCHES CAMPAIGN URGING AOC TO RUN FOR PRESIDENT WHILE PROGRESSIVES EYE SOCIALIST CANDIDATE Ocasio-Cortez, who has drawn support from the Democratic Socialists of America's (DSA) New York City chapter for a potential White House bid, emphasized her desire to advance legislation in the 120th Congress rather than focus on presidential politics. Asked whether Democrats should work with Trump instead of prioritizing impeachment proceedings and congressional investigations, Ocasio-Cortez expressed optimism about finding common ground. "I hope so," she told Fox News Digital. "You know, I hope that President Trump can sign a congressional stock trading ban into law," Ocasio-Cortez continued. The congresswoman also identified healthcare reform as a potential area for bipartisan cooperation, urging Trump to address changes to Medicaid that she warned could threaten coverage for millions of Americans. DOZENS OF HOUSE DEMOCRATS REJECT BILL FUSING CONGRESSIONAL STOCK BAN WITH FEDERAL VOTER ID "I hope President Trump will be willing to work with us in really adjusting this Medicaid and confronting this Medicaid cliff that stands to kick off millions of working Americans off of their healthcare," she said. "And so, you know, there are going to be areas where we're going to have real disagreement and real confrontation or worse," she continued. Despite those disagreements, Ocasio-Cortez argued that lawmakers should prioritize legislation addressing Americans' immediate concerns. "My hope is that we can prioritize the things that can actually change people's lives for the better as quickly as possible," she said. Her remarks came hours after House Democrats overwhelmingly nominated Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., for speaker of the 120th Congress. At least five of the 11 Democrats who opposed Jeffries’ nomination are incoming Congress members and self-described democratic socialists who argued that the party's leadership does not adequately represent their political priorities. JEFFRIES SURVIVES DEM VOTE TO SECURE SPEAKER POSITION AS PROGRESSIVE RESISTANCE CLOUDS HIS CHANCES Ocasio-Cortez, a DSA member, acknowledged that ideological disagreements between Jeffries and the party's socialist wing could continue throughout the next Congress. "Of course, there are going to be areas where leader Jeffries and DSA are going to be in strong opposition," Ocasio-Cortez told Fox News Digital. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP However, she expressed confidence that Democrats could unite around shared priorities, including expanding access to publicly funded healthcare. Her comments highlight the competing pressures facing House Democrats as they prepare to govern with a new majority while balancing progressive policy demands, internal ideological divisions and potential opportunities to work with the Trump administration. Jeffries did not respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

articles.title: Will the midterm mandate bring real change?
articles.summary: Following the Nov. 3 midterm elections, the incoming Congress faces intense political maneuvering as House Republicans elect Jim Jordan as minority leader and Democrats prepare to advance legislative priorities such as healthcare reform and investigations into the Trump administration.
articles.body:
Gaius Petronius Arbiter, a first century A.D. Roman author, observed that change for the sake of change is an illusion of progress. That insight rattled around my mind while reflecting on the Nov. 3 midterm elections.

After a week of “reckoning” what the Democratic sweep of the tables at all levels of government meant for the parties, their members and the nation at large, the new watchword became “change.” The American people voted for change in the government, the parties, and national policy priorities. But what kind of change, by and for whom, and at what cost and perils going into the 2028 presidential election?

Certainly, no one wants to fall into the Petronius trap of fighting for change for its own sake, only to be called on it by voters at the next election for having merely created the illusion of progress.

In my previous column , I expressed skepticism that things would change much in the new Congress with basically the same leadership and many of the same burned-out incumbents still stuck in the same-old rut of battling and blaming each other instead of tackling the major problems facing most Americans.

I held out a slim hope that the roughly 120 newly elected House members and handful of new senators might shake-up the place enough to force the leadership to change its ways and listen to what the people have really been demanding.

Neither the bipartisan new member orientation last week on the Hill nor the humongous gathering of Democrats at the “What Next?” conference in Denver that followed have produced convincing signs of new directions and priorities — other than that everyone can now pronounce the word “change.” Nor have the party leadership races so far demonstrated different directions. It was still the same old internal finger pointing and blame gaming.

House Republicans did make one change in leadership, voting to elect Rep. Jim Jordan (Ohio), a combative conservative, as their new minority leader over incumbent Republican leader Steve Scalise (La.). Jordan indicated his priority as minority leader will be to protect President Trump against all the investigations Democrats have vowed to unleash.

In House Democratic leadership elections Wednesday, current Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (N.Y.) was elected, by a secret ballot vote of 251 to 11 , as the majority caucus’s nominee for Speaker, despite some grumbling in the ranks. Other sitting leaders were elevated a notch on the ladder without opposition.

In the Senate, Republican Leader John Thune (S.D.) was reelected party leader without opposition, though his raucous caucus members went through three meetings in a single day to air their grievances before reelecting their entire leadership team.

The Senate Democratic leadership votes will not take place until Dec. 1. Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.), 67, is challenging incumbent Minority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.), 75, for the majority leader slot. Van Hollen is running on the mantra that it’s time for a new generation of leadership that can deliver real change. Schumer is touting his success in delivering a Senate majority. As Sen. Angus King (I-Maine) put it, “ Why would you fire the manager when you just won the World Series? ”

High on the Democratic list of legislative priorities in the new Congress will be healthcare reforms, immigration law changes, tariffs, and ending the Iran war. Details to follow. President Trump announced even prior to the midterm election that he will become “ Mr. Veto ” if Democrats capture the Congress.

Democrats are also poised to launch a whole series of investigations of the Trump administration. As Rep. Robert Garcia (D-Calif.), the prospective new chairman of the House Oversight and Government Reform Committee advised the president and his Cabinet members, “ Lawyer up .” The administration has reportedly already added 15 lawyers to the Whie House counsel’s office in anticipation of a boatload of subpoenas and contempt citations.

One might expect some hint of the midterm election impact on members’ behavior as they wrap-up the work of the current Congress. High on the list of unfinished business are all 12 appropriations bills which have been backstopped by a continuing resolution at current year spending levels, which expires on Dec. 11.

Several options are available: enacting an omnibus appropriations bill through next September; another short-term continuing resolution into early next year; or a government shutdown if no compromise can be reached between the House, Senate and the White House.

The latter prospect takes us full circle to the embarrassing government closure last year and defies any sign that real change is in the air — not even an illusion of progress.

Don Wolfensberger is a 28-year congressional staff veteran, culminating as chief of staff of the House Rules Committee. He is author of “Congress and the People: Deliberative Democracy on Trial” and “Changing Cultures in Congress: From Fair Play to Power Plays.”

articles.title: Musk says he’s ‘not MAGA’
articles.summary: Tech mogul Elon Musk said Wednesday that he does not associate himself with President Trump’s “Make America Great Again” (MAGA) movement, a notable statement given his closeness to the president. “My motivations were very simple, which is just to sort of have, like, one of either, the House, Senate or presidency be Republican in ’29,…
articles.body:
Tech mogul Elon Musk said Wednesday that he does not associate himself with President Trump’s “Make America Great Again” (MAGA) movement, a notable statement given his closeness to the president.

“My motivations were very simple, which is just to sort of have, like, one of either, the House, Senate or presidency be Republican in ’29, and not have just a sort of, in the worst-case scenario, a supermajority of Democrats,” Musk said of his recent spending in the midterm elections in an interview with Andrew Ross Sorkin at The New York Times DealBook Summit.

“I’m not in favor of a supermajority of Republicans either. You know, I think we have some — want to have some checks and balances here. That was it, really. So, you know, I think I’m ideologically quite moderate,” the tech leader added.

Musk went on later to say he is “not MAGA,” adding that “at least I’m not like — I’m not sure what MAGA means, but I don’t think I’m like, if that means sort of blind adherence to a set of policies by the Republican Party, then I certainly don’t have that.”

“I think there are positives and negatives in both parties,” he continued.

Musk also said Wednesday that he felt “pretty foolish” after spending $442 million on Republican campaigns in this year’s midterms, in which Democrats won both the House and Senate. The tech mogul told Sorkin that he had a goal of Republicans keeping the Senate.

“I feel pretty foolish about having spent so much money and not seeing much for it,” Musk told Sorkin. “Or maybe it would’ve been much worse without that. But it certainly shows that American elections are not just about money. Obviously you can put a lot of money into an election and have an effect that is relatively minor, and I think that was the case here.”

Musk had a close relationship with Trump amid the run-up to the 2024 presidential election and spent time in the president’s second administration heading up the Department of Government Efficiency.

After a brief falling-out following Musk’s exit from the White House last year, he and the president have rekindled their friendship .

articles.title: White House takes phones from reporters traveling from China with president
articles.summary: Reporters traveling with President Trump had their phones taken away as they departed China on Thursday. A report from the pool reporter said, “Our phones are being taken away for now for security reasons.” The news that phones were taken away from reporters quickly circulated online, sparking theories over why the security step was taken.…
articles.body:
Reporters traveling with President Trump had their phones taken away as they departed China on Thursday.

A report from the pool reporter said, “Our phones are being taken away for now for security reasons.”

The news that phones were taken away from reporters quickly circulated online, sparking theories over why the security step was taken.

The White House did not provide a more specific public explanation for why phones were taken away. The Hill has reached out to the White House for comment.

Trump told NBC’s Gabe Gutierrez in a phone call that “we want to be careful, and we didn’t want to have people have phones when they shouldn’t have phones, so we were very careful.”

A note from the TV pooler , shared online from CBS’s Jennifer Jacobs, said an Air Force One aide collected White House staffers’ burner phones and asked journalists to place the phones they used in China in signal-blocking bags until they land back in the U.S.

Some journalists had already put their devices in the bags before landing in China, according to the official.

“Many (but not all) reporters and photographers had placed their regular work phones, personal phones, laptops and smart watches in metal-lined bags to prevent potential spyware, surveillance or data collection and are able to use them on the flight to the US,” the note reads. “Those who hadn’t opted for burners were left with no cellphone.”

The president departed from the Shenzhen Bao’an International Airport on Thursday evening local time in China.

Trump was in Asia for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations summit in the Philippines and the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in China.

Earlier in the day, Trump participated in a bilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping, a pull-aside meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin and a trilateral meeting with Xi and Putin.

A Bloomberg reporter asked a question during the bilateral meeting with Xi and was subsequently barred from entering the trilateral meeting by China.

When Trump was in China in May, the traveling reporters complained about aggression from the Chinese reporters.

Reporters traveling with the president at that time did not have their phones taken away when they departed. Instead, the press pool said officials took everything that was given to them by the Chinese, like press credentials, burner phones and delegation pins.

articles.title: A course correction with lessons for both parties
articles.summary: Rep. James E. Clyburn reflects on the 2026 midterm elections, noting how Democratic victories in several Southern states signaled a voter mandate for accessible services, affordable programs, and accountable representation.
articles.body:
In the midterm elections, voters handed Democrats a three-prong mandate to give the American people services that are accessible, programs that are affordable, and representation that is accountable.

Throughout the campaign, I often uttered the notion (attributed to Alexis De Tocqueville, although disputed by some historians) that “America is great because she is good,” and that “if America ever ceases to be good, she will cease to be great.”

The notion of goodness was an undercurrent that ran rampant throughout this campaign cycle. I was reminded of that while campaigning with U.S. Sen.-elect Scott Colom (D-Miss.), in Ruleville, Miss. As I greeted people at the Fannie Lou Hamer Memorial, I heard yearnings for accessible healthcare and childcare, affordable housing and energy, and accountable representation.

I heard expressions of Fannie Lou Hamer’s famous axiom of being “sick and tired” of the government’s failures. Those concerns are not unique to Ruleville, nor are they limited to government officials’ callousness toward Americans.

I campaigned throughout 14 states with a firm understanding of what was at stake. In “Democracy in America,” Alexis De Tocqueville wrote, “The greatness of America lies not in being more enlightened than any other nation but rather in her ability to repair her faults.” I was hopeful that most Americans were ready to repair the faultlines that have erupted from the election of President Trump to a second term.

During the 2020 elections, I was writing my third book, “The First Eight.” I intended for the book to be some light-hearted facts about the eight Black congressmen who served in Congress from South Carolina before me. But after I saw President Trump and his supporters react to his defeat by Joe Biden, I recognized what was happening in Detroit and Philadelphia, and with that “perfect” telephone call down to Georgia . Trump and MAGA extremists were trying to stop the counting of votes and alter the Electoral College results to throw the election into the House of Representatives.

Although they failed to stop the counting, they did not cease. Those failures led to the Jan. 6, 2021, insurrection. When that failed, they continued their efforts to subvert the will of the voting public. Those efforts resulted in “Project 2025” which I referred to — in real time — as “Jim Crow 2.0.”

But on Nov. 3, America delivered an echo of Fannie Lou Hamer’s Dec. 20, 1964, assertion, which she concludes with “we want a change.”

Scott Colom is the first African American popularly elected to represent Mississippi in the United States Senate. This race was called eight days after Election Day, due in large measure, to the lack of civility displayed by Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith (R-Miss.) when she prematurely declared victory on election night, being very dismissive of Colom and vitriolic of the moment.

Two African Americans, Hiram R. Revels and Blanche Bruce , represented Mississippi in the United States Senate during Reconstruction and post-Reconstruction. Until 1913, many U.S. senators were elected by their state’s legislatures. Senators were not popularly elected until the 17th Amendment to the Constitution was adopted . But what makes the success of Scott Colom relevant to this discussion are the congressional interactions that led to his candidacy.

Rep. Bennie Thompson (D-Miss.) recommended Colom for a federal Judgeship for which he was eminently qualified, and President Joe Biden nominated him. But despite Thompson’s and Biden’s best efforts and broad bipartisan support for Colom among Mississippians, Hyde-Smith used her senatorial privileges to un-ceremoniously deny him the judgeship.

Her treatment of Colom was unwarranted and mean. I do not know if she would have had an opponent for reelection if she had allowed a vote on Colom’s confirmation, but I doubt it. And even if she had, it certainly would not have been Colom.

The midterm election results are history, but they exposed some lessons that need to be learned by both parties. As for my side of the aisle, hopefully we have learned not to ignore the South in the future. We have a lot of hard workers in our party who are devoted to making our government work for everybody. But there are some in our party who seem to be oblivious to some realities.

Over half of the nation’s African Americans live in the South, the fastest growing region of the country. America’s fastest growing county is in my congressional district, and South Carolina is arguably the country’s fastest growing state. To be successful in electoral politics, we must take our campaigns to where the votes are. On Election Day, South Carolina, Texas, Georgia, Mississippi, and North Carolina, all states in the American South, proved that.

In my home state of South Carolina, Dr. Annie Andrews became the first woman elected to serve in the U.S. Senate. Vice Admiral Nancy Lacore flipped South Carolina’s 1st District from red to blue and now joins me in the U.S. House of Representatives. The results of our governor’s race and the other congressional races were much closer than expected, but results I had hoped and worked for years.

While the voters of the 2026 midterm election gave Democrats a three-prong mandate on accessibility, affordability and accountability — they also offered my friends on the other side of the aisle an opportunity to gain some new perspectives. Hopefully, they will accept some advice from one who is genuinely southern and proudly Black.

People do not respond favorably to insults and bad manners. Telling southern legislators what they must do, and Blacks what they must accept, are not winning propositions. We do not believe the country is in need of being made great. We think it already is great.

The greatness of this nation is measured not simply by its power or prosperity, but by the character and compassion of its people, the dignity and respect we render to one another, and our willingness to recognize that, even when we disagree, we are all Americans in search of a “more perfect Union.”

James E. Clyburn represents South Carolina’s 6th District in Congress. From 2011 to 2018 and 2023 to March 2024, he served as assistant Democratic leader. He served as House majority whip from 2019 to 2022.

articles.title: Ben Shapiro casts doubt on possible Vance 2028 bid: ‘He’s extraordinarily online’
articles.summary: Conservative commentator Ben Shapiro threw cold water on the notion of a presidential bid for Vice President Vance, saying he has doubts that Vance would be able to successfully “duplicate” President Trump’s coalition to win in 2028. “I think that’s the gravest mistake actually that any Republican or Democratic politician can make, it to say…
articles.body:
Conservative commentator Ben Shapiro threw cold water on the notion of a presidential bid for Vice President Vance, saying he has doubts that Vance would be able to successfully “duplicate” President Trump’s coalition to win in 2028.

“I think that’s the gravest mistake actually that any Republican or Democratic politician can make, it to say my predecessor had this coalition, therefore I will duplicate the coalition,” Shapiro told NPR . “If JD Vance tries to do that … that’s not going to work either.”

Shapiro said he does not think the vice president would be able to expand Trump’s winning coalition from 2024, which was largely made up of rural white voters, young voters and Latino voters. The latter two swung hard to Republicans in 2024 and back to Democrats in 2026.

“I look at the coalition that the vice president is relying upon, and it looks like a much smaller version of the same coalition that President Trump had,” Shapiro said. “Does he do better with Hispanics than Trump did in 2024? There’s no way.”

Shapiro also said he thinks Vance would perform worse with blue-collar white voters, married women, single women and college-educated voters.

Asked why Shapiro thought Vance would perform poorly, Shapiro said he thought the vice president was too focused on niche audiences, like young men and “podcast bros.”

“I think he’s extraordinarily online. I think the vice president spends an inordinate amount of time worrying what the podcast bros think,” Shapiro said. “I think his entire effect has been … in ways that are designed to appeal to 21-year-old Joe Rogan listeners. And I think that is not how you win a broadscale national election.”

Vance is considered a front-runner for the 2028 Republican presidential nomination, even as he publicly maintains that he has not decided whether he will run.

He increased speculation that he may jump into the race just after big GOP losses in the midterms, when he put out a post on the social platform X blaming the Iran war for his party’s defeat. Vance was previously skeptical of U.S. entanglement in foreign conflicts but has had to defend the Iran war despite its unpopularity.

The vice president’s likely main rival, should they both choose to run, would be Secretary of State Marco Rubio.

Rubio has grown in favorability and preference among Republicans in recent months. A new Emerson College poll found Rubio winning the support of 36 percent of Republican primary voters — 30 points higher from last year’s result — and Vance winning 20 percent, a 20-point drop.

Shapiro said he thinks the secretary would be a much better candidate than Vance.

“I look over at Secretary of State Rubio and what I see there is, I don’t know if he would win, but I know his coalition would look different,” Shapiro said. “For the vice president, I see pretty much all the Trump knobs turned down. And with the secretary of State, I see some knobs turned way up and some turned down.”

articles.title: New Congress must continue the important work of the China Committee
articles.summary: Incoming House leadership should maintain the Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party to address ongoing national security threats and economic risks posed by Beijing.
articles.body:
Following the midterm elections, Washington is poised for change. But the incoming House majority should act smartly when writing its new rules in January. In particular, members should continue the work of the Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party. Incoming House Speaker Hakeem Jeffries (D-N.Y.) has said he will consult with Democratic leaders about the future of the China committee. But given the serious challenges posed by an aggressive Beijing, it should be a no-brainer to keep the committee going.

By the time the select committee was established in 2023, the U.S. had already lost an estimated 3.8 million jobs due to China’s massive subsidization of state-owned industries. And so, if Democrats want to follow their longstanding practice of supporting American labor, they should prioritize the committee’s work.

The primary objection to the China committee appears to be an ongoing turf battle among lawmakers. Standing committees — including Foreign Affairs, Armed Services, Financial Services, and Energy and Commerce — share some overlap in terms of foreign policy. However, the select committee is the only one specifically focused on threats posed by Beijing. In fact, it cannot even report bills. Instead, it investigates and submits findings to the House and relevant standing committees.

Given the recent clamor over chipmaker Nvidia — and the possibility of proprietary U.S. technology being compromised by Chinese actors — the committee’s work is particularly timely. Consider the committee’s DeepSeek investigation , which found that a Chinese AI platform had funneled American user data to Beijing. In particular, the committee found that DeepSeek relied on restricted Nvidia chips.

The China committee has also been at the forefront of telecommunications concerns . One committee investigation found that China Telecom, China Mobile and China Unicom have all retained connections to America’s internet infrastructure even after their authorizations were denied or revoked. And the committee’s “Minerals Mafia” investigation documented 14 cases of corruption, environmental destruction, and human rights abuses by Chinese mining companies, including a previously suppressed report on a waste spill in Zambia.

These are critical investigations that deliver actionable information for Congress’s standing committees. Earlier this year, the select committee’s research on Chinese acquisition of advanced AI capabilities led to the MATCH Act , which will strengthen controls on semiconductor manufacturing. Similarly, bipartisan legislation by committee Chair John Moolenaar (R-Mich.) helped strengthen the Federal Acquisition Security Council. And new investment restrictions , including the Biosecure Act, became law in the fiscal 2026 National Defense Authorization Act.

There’s still much to tackle, however. Beijing’s leverage over critical minerals has put America’s industrial security at risk. China’s rare earth export controls have already forced some U.S. automakers to reduce or suspend production. And Beijing maintains other serious chokepoints, something the committee continues to investigate.

If congressional Democrats want to protect America’s families, they should be encouraging the China committee’s work — particularly when it comes to essential medicines. The United States is now heavily dependent on pharmaceutical production in China; the committee has led multiple investigations into unsafe drug imports.

Cybersecurity is another concern. Recent hacks of European supermarket refrigeration systems make clear the seriousness of cybersecurity threats on commercial equipment. According to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, Chinese AI was used in these cyber attacks — something that warrants immediate congressional scrutiny.

Labor unions in America are hoping Congress will continue the committee’s work. Earlier this month, the United Auto Workers urged House leaders to retain the committee, citing concerns over China’s heavily subsidized electric vehicle production.

The incoming House majority should preserve the committee’s bipartisan character and existing jurisdictions. Renewing the committee would help Congress retain its most dedicated forum for investigations across policy boundaries even as standing committees continue to lead in their respective areas.

The seriousness of Beijing’s strategic threats should not be overlooked, and lawmakers should never play partisan politics when it comes to national security. That’s why the Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party must be maintained — and play a useful role in the consequential work ahead.

EJ Valentine is director of government relations for the Coalition for a Prosperous America.

articles.title: Buttigieg supporters unveil Team Pete PAC ahead of 2028 vote
articles.summary: Supporters of former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg launched a new fundraising committee Thursday to push the former presidential candidate to run again in 2028. The new Team Pete PAC is made up of a group of former Buttigieg campaign volunteers and is not affiliated with him personally. “Whether they originally knocked doors for him in…
articles.body:
Supporters of former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg launched a new fundraising committee Thursday to push the former presidential candidate to run again in 2028.

The new Team Pete PAC is made up of a group of former Buttigieg campaign volunteers and is not affiliated with him personally.

“Whether they originally knocked doors for him in 2020 or just turned up the volume when he appeared on Fox News, our supporters want to do more than urge him to run,” Team Pete co-founder Jennifer Holdsworth said in a release. “If Pete runs, he’ll have a team in every corner of the country already showing that a more positive politics is possible.”

Buttigieg has leaned into speculation that he may launch another presidential campaign. The former South Bend, Ind., mayor frequently appears on Fox News to defend his positions; he campaigned for Democrats around the country in the midterms and announced the release of his new book on reforming the American political system. Since his 2020 campaign, he has become a father and grown a beard.

And even as most presidential hopefuls deny speculation about their potential candidacy, Buttigieg has been more upfront; the former secretary said in August that he was “more inclined than not” to run for president in 2028.

Some polls show him in a solid position with strong favorability among his party’s voters.

A recent Reuters/Ipsos poll of Democratic voters showed Buttigieg and Sen. Jon Ossoff (D-Ga.) receiving the highest marks from voters. Each candidate had 29 percent of Democrats saying they would make an excellent presidential candidate. A combined 56 percent of the party’s voters said Buttigieg would make an excellent or good candidate, the highest support of any candidate surveyed.

Buttigieg shocked many when he won the Iowa caucuses in 2020 despite entering the race with low name recognition and little political experience.

But a reshaped Democratic presidential primary calendar may not play to Buttigieg’s strengths as a candidate. The former secretary struggled with Black voters in his last campaign, and the first state on the primary calendar in 2028 is South Carolina, where Black voters make up a large share of Democratic primary voters.

No major candidate has announced a 2028 run yet, but historically, campaigns have launched in the weeks and months after the midterm elections.

articles.title: Hometown of accused US military plane saboteur is a known magnet for anti-Israel activism
articles.summary: Cork, Ireland, hometown of Daithí O’Corráin, who faces U.S. charges of destroying a $60 million C-130, once banned Benjamin Netanyahu from its city limits.
articles.body: The European hometown of the man who single-handedly destroyed a U.S. military transport aircraft in an act of apparent protest has a rich history of pro-Palestinian support. This includes the town council for Cork, Ireland, barring Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu from entering its city limits, citing his "illegal occupation of Palestine and bordering countries" and the continuous pro-Palestinian protests taking place every Saturday since October 2023, organized by the Cork Palestine Solidarity Campaign (CPSC). Cork’s opposition to Israel adds context to the possible motives for why Daithí O’Corráin, an Irish national, allegedly destroyed a U.S. military C-130 Hercules aircraft in April. The incident also draws attention to several anti-Israel groups that have sprung up in Ireland in recent years. IRELAND’S ELITES HAVE FOUND THEIR NEW RELIGION: HATING ISRAEL Ireland’s anti-Israel foothold became international news in April when O’Corráin, a Cork native, barricaded himself inside a C-130, a U.S. military transport plane. Once inside, he tore out critical wiring, destroyed gauges, contaminated fuel tanks and even poured corrosive chemicals into the aircraft, according to the U.S. Department of Justice. Although his motives remain unclear, several groups from Cork interpreted his actions as a form of resistance against Israel and U.S. military interventionism. In one such case, a Cork business owner named Tracey Ryan launched an initiative to raise €20,000 for O’Corráin's legal defense, praising his efforts to resist "the unwanted presence of U.S. military in Ireland in the face of their illegal war & support of Israel’s genocide." "We, Daithí's friends and comrades, are raising funds to support him through his court case. We would really appreciate your support & will keep you updated here on ways to support Daithí," Ryan wrote in the description of the fundraising page. According to her personal Facebook profile, Ryan joined a bus of pro-Palestinian activists who went to support O’Corráin at his court appearance. "Bus going to the high court to support Daithí on Thursday!!" Ryan wrote. O’Corráin has also received support from CPSC, the Cork pro-Palestinian group. As news of the incident spread, CPSC co-chair Anne McShane posted on her Palestinian advocacy Facebook page in support of O’Corráin, encouraging viewers to send him letters of encouragement after his incarceration. "Daithi needs our support in order to keep up his morale. Letters are a lifeline for prisoners," an April 17 post read. CPSC spearheads anti-Israel demonstrations in Cork. In addition to hosting several pro-Palestinian fundraising initiatives, the group facilitates weekly Saturday demonstrations and invites speakers. At one point, CPSC’s website featured a fundraising site for O’Corráin, but the page has since been removed. INSIDE THE PROTEST PLAYBOOK TO VILIFY ISRAEL ON 'GLOBAL DAY OF ACTION' In CPSC’s own words, the group is part of a larger pro-Palestinian movement. "It’s not just the city. Towns across all of County Cork stand in solidarity with Palestinians, including Ballincollig, Bandon, Cobh, Charleville, Clonakilty, Fermoy, Kinsale, Macroom, Mallow, Mitchelstown, Skibbereen and more," the group states on its website. "Cork Palestine Solidarity Campaign is a branch of the Irish Palestine Solidarity Campaign (IPSC)," it added. As part of its sister groups’ efforts "to foster links between Palestine and Irish institutions and organizations," CPSC and IPSC have both applauded Cork’s city council efforts to promote pro-Palestinian policies. "Well done to the Cork City Council which passed a motion … calling for the Central Bank to end the sale of Israeli bonds," one Facebook post reads. The groups have also held Cork up as a template for Ireland’s national policy. "We call on the Irish government to follow the example of both Dublin and Cork city councils by officially recognizing Israeli Apartheid – and acting to end any and all links to this regime," another statement reads. For its own part, the Cork City Council has earned the support of IPSC and CPSC through a range of its official resolutions, making the town’s formal position to condemn any of Ireland’s ties to Israel. In addition to banning Netanyahu from entering the city's limits in a 41-8 vote in 2024, Cork’s council has flown the Palestinian flag over city hall on U.N. International Day of Solidarity and called on Ireland to ban trade from Israeli settlements. Cork has even passed a "twinning" mechanism with the Palestinian city of Nablus — a largely symbolic partnership. IRISH PM REJECTS ANTISEMITISM CONCERNS IN IRELAND AMID DRAMATIC VOTE OVER BOYCOTTING ISRAEL GAME Fergal Dennehy, the lord mayor of Cork from 2025 to 2026, hosted the mayor of Nablus in February, calling the partnership "just the beginning of what we hope will be a wonderful relationship between our two great cities." Neither CPSC nor Cork City Council responded to Fox News Digital's requests for comment on the city's pro-Palestinian positions or about connections to O’Corráin. articles.title: ‘Long term coup’ ousted Christians, conservatives from major watchdog, insider claims
articles.summary: A former SPLC director told FBI agents Christians and conservatives were pushed out first in what he called a "long-term coup" at the Southern Poverty Law Center.
articles.body: A former Southern Poverty Law Center official who led its hate-group tracking work told FBI agents he tried to make the watchdog’s controversial "Hate Map" more ideologically balanced, while saying Christians and conservatives were the first staffers pushed out in what he called a "long-term coup" at the organization after he left in 2013. The former director said he pushed for a more evenhanded SPLC, arguing that its "Hate Map" — which lists conservative groups alongside Ku Klux Klan chapters — should also include left-wing extremists, including violent animal-rights and extremist environmental groups. However, the former director said the effort met resistance and that, as liberal leaders reshaped the organization, most of his 17-person team was replaced. "There was some kind of coup, long-term coup going on there between some, what I would — what I heard were some pretty liberal people, extreme people that had other ideas about what we were doing," the unnamed former director told agents, as first reported by The Daily Signal's Tyler O'Neil, who has been covering the SPLC's legal troubles. DOJ EXPANDS INDICTMENT AGAINST SPLC, ALLEGING $4M SECRETLY FUNNELED TO KKK AND EXTREMIST GROUPS The former director’s comments appeared in an FBI interview transcript filed as an exhibit to Dr. Heidi Beirich’s Nov. 2 court filing. Beirich, a former SPLC official charged alongside the organization in a federal case alleging a scheme to mislead donors and banks about donations used to pay informants associated with violent extremist groups, pointed to multiple FBI interviews with an unnamed former SPLC director, identified in the filing as "Individual-1." In a January interview, Individual-1 told investigators he ran the SPLC’s field-source program, set up accounts used to pay sources and directed payments, according to Beirich’s filing. During a March 23 follow-up interview with Individual-1, FBI Special Agents David McDaniel and Parker Still framed the conversation around the program having "gone off the rails" under Beirich and told the former director they were not there to discuss the bank activity, noting he had "obviously nothing to do with all that," before questioning him about the SPLC’s alleged targeting of conservative organizations and Beirich’s role, according to the transcript. EXCLUSIVE: SPLC'S 'FAR-LEFT,' 'ANTI-RACISM' CURRICULUM FOUND IN CLASSROOMS AS EARLY AS KINDERGARTEN: 'WATCHDOG' Individual-1 responded that, as his "gut impression," he believed her actions were political and accused some liberals at the center of having "a good degree of hatred" for conservatism, according to the March 23 transcript. Individual-1 also alleged a shift in power at the SPLC. After he left in 2013, he said, people were appointed to the SPLC’s board as "figureheads" and eventually gained enough voting power to take over the center. He said only one or two data-entry members of his roughly 17-person team remained, with the others replaced by staff he believed shared the new leadership’s politics. "That's who they ran off first were the Christians and conservatives," the unnamed former director told agents when asked why Beirich took the actions she did after his departure. "Then they — then the rest they just replaced with people they liked, you know, that agreed with them politically." HOW MUTINY AT SOUTHERN POVERTY LAW CENTER TRIGGERED LEADERSHIP COLLAPSE In separate comments about the SPLC's controversial "Hate Map," Individual-1 said he persuaded SPLC staff, despite internal resistance, to list Black separatist groups, which he considered comparable to White racist groups, on the map. However, he said he unsuccessfully pushed the SPLC to include violent animal-rights and environmental extremist groups and described his team’s approach during his tenure as director as "very nonpartisan" and "middle of the road." "We were very nonpartisan, or at least when I was running things, when I was director, we stayed right in the middle of the road," he said. In a June follow-up, the unnamed former director also criticized the SPLC's "Hate Map" for listing local chapters separately, saying it made the map's totals of the extremist groups it chose to identify look larger. WATCH: SPLC CHIEF DOUBLES DOWN ON PLACING CHARLIE KIRK'S TURNING POINT USA ON 'HATE MAP' While the unnamed former director was not charged in the SPLC case, Beirich was. Her lawyers say the interviews with the unnamed director warrant discovery into whether she was singled out because of her perceived role in the SPLC’s political speech, arguing that investigators’ questions about the SPLC’s treatment of conservative groups — and her alleged role in that work — could show the prosecution was motivated by hostility to the center’s political speech. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "Individual-1’s statements confirm my longstanding criticism of the Southern Poverty Law Center, that it exaggerates ‘hate’ by inflating the chapters on its ‘hate map’ and that it systematically demonizes conservatives and Christians while turning a blind eye to extremism on the Left," O’Neil, the author of "Making Hate Pay: The Corruption of the Southern Poverty Law Center," told Fox News Digital. "Now, we have the former director of the Intelligence Project saying the SPLC appears to have pushed out Christians and conservatives, while rejecting his suggestion to include environmentalist agitators on the map."
